To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a comprehensive approach for prediction and evaluation of power system transient instability in real-time can be developed by combining post-disturbance PMU data with a finite difference based approach for prediction of rotor angles and data-mining based clustering to identify the critical machines, which are then transformed to a SMIB system for the evaluation of transient instability in terms of unstable margins and time to instability.

a new approach for prediction and evaluation of transient stability in power systems based on the data acquired by PMUs is proposed, and its performance is demonstrated on the New England 10 machine system.

the proposed method is capable of identifying the most critical machines, which are the ones most likely to lose synchronism, and predicting unstable conditions, i.e. time to instability, with high accuracy.

the following objectives: 1) development of an approach that exploits PMU data for prediction and evaluation of system transient stability in the post-disturbence time frame, 2) identification of critical machines in the post-disturbing system, and 3) assessment of the unstable margin and time of the critical machines.
the development of a comprehensive approach for prediction and evaluation of the transient stability of a power system in real-time.
the development of a comprehensive approach for prediction and evaluation of transient stability in real time.
